$comment: jitLLM's source lock (D-017, D-057): every third-party source component a build may use, with its exact bytes, license classification and build options. third_party/README.md describes the schema and how to change it.
`mise run prepare` fetches and unpacks the selected components into build/sources; configure (cmake/JitllmSources.cmake) only consumes those trees and writes the build receipt.

license.scope: Only cuda/mmq/ds4_mmq_d2r.cu and its header, built by the patched jitllm/CMakeLists.txt as jitllm_ds4_d2r in CUDA profiles (an empty interface target in CPU profiles). The unit contains Q2_K down, IQ2_XXS paired/fused and dense Q8 D2R kernels; native dispatch calls only the new raw-Q2_K down launcher. The patch reconstructs the original shared weight tile directly from raw GGUF blocks at native padded strides, keeps the original D2R integer-MMA/scatter arithmetic and adds no permanent SoA replica. Includes common.cuh and mmq.cuh resolve to independently locked GGML, not ds4's vendored shims. Only the patched CMake file executes; no upstream runtime, graph, cache, routing, repack, dispatcher, tools or original build script is kept or executed.

ggml.verification: Pinned to llama.cpp tag b10964 (also v0.4.1), commit b29c606e28a01b1bc8c1351026a0fa6e616bf6c4, the revision of the FP16 reference and toolchain bridge (docs/experiments/first-slice/pins.json, docs/experiments/backend-proof-p0/). GitHub's archive of that commit was downloaded twice on 2026-09-26 with identical SHA-256 and size. tree_sha256 is the kept, patched tree, computed by the shared tools/jitllm_sources.py validator during preparation, configure and build. Patches 0001/0002's adaptations are selected by GGML_JITLLM and jitllm/CMakeLists.txt. Patch 0004 adds default-off compact routed MMQ tile lists and corrects dummy-column scratch padding in the ordinary routed Q8/FP4 preparation; original MMQ arithmetic and raw strides are retained. Patch 0003 narrowly backports sparse query-tile unions/live counts from llama.cpp PRs 28770/29298 for jitLLM's own flash-attention launchers; the original fattn.cu is not compiled. The build reproduces the bridge's flags for these files (-O3, sm_121a SASS, -use_fast_math, -extended-lambda, C11/C++17 host code, C++17 CUDA); the bridge's compile commands are the reference. The x86-64 native build also compiles them for its discrete GPUs' SASS (sm_86, D-082), beside and without changing sm_121a's. M3 (2026-09-28) widened the compiled set for DeepSeek V4 Flash and Qwen3.8 Flash; the operations' results were compared with FP64 references on a GB10 within upstream's test-backend-ops bounds (tests/unit/ggml_ext_ops_test.cc). The ds4 study (2026-09-29) adds IQ2_XXS/Q2_K instances and the sparse backport, checked on the same GB10 with random overlapping/disjoint masks, partial query tiles, empty sink rows and finite mask biases.

Against the gated exl3_moe_coop_kernel.cuh, hadamard_inner.cuh shares a 66-token Hadamard butterfly that it already held before that kernel arrived (58d4d73) (checked 2026-09-27; docs/licensing.md).

exllamav3.verification: Pinned to commit 6b84a21b6f1e5da3f291b9e1019061f0de788279 (2026-09-20, one commit after tag v1.5.1), the revision of the EXL3 reference and the P0 bridge (docs/experiments/exl3-reference/pins.json, docs/experiments/backend-proof-p0/). GitHub's archive of that commit was downloaded twice on 2026-09-27 with identical SHA-256 and size; its 743 files are byte-identical to the commit's Git tree. tree_sha256 is the kept, patched tree, computed by the shared tools/jitllm_sources.py validator during preparation, configure and build. The patches (third_party/patches/exllamav3/) remove util.cuh's exiting error checks (inline header code, so no guard macro could keep them out of every translation unit that includes it), drop six no-op `register` specifiers that NVCC rejects with a Clang host compiler, add jitLLM's build and instance unit, and remove the ATen host wrappers from the three sources whose kernels the native linear launches. The build reproduces the P0 reference's device flags (NVCC 13.4.92, -O3 --use_fast_math, sm_121 SASS, C++20, PyTorch's half-operator macros and --expt-relaxed-constexpr; the x86-64 native build adds its discrete GPUs' SASS, sm_86, D-082): every ExLlamaV3 function the native sweep's binary holds (the 64 GEMM and multi-GEMM instances and the instance unit's 29) has SASS identical, text and encodings, to its namesake in the reference extension built by NVCC 13.4.92 (aa8b9f16...), the 27 the per-linear sweep launches among them (cuobjdump 13.0.85 on spark-b, 2026-09-27; docs/experiments/backend-proof-p3/).
